newsitem.title: UK: Former UK minister to fight on in Conservative row.
newsitem.headline: Former UK minister to fight on in Conservative row.

text.p: A former minister locked in battle with Michael Howard, the former Home Secretary now vying for the leadership of the ousted Conservatives, vowed to fight on after her hopes of a parliamentary debate were dashed on Thursday.

Ann Widdecombe, junior minister in charge of prisons under Howard until Labour's landslide election victory two weeks ago, told Reuters the House of Commons speaker had refused her permission to make a personal statement to the House of Commons. But Widdecombe, whose bitter squabble with Howard has overshadowed the Conservative leadership race, said she would try to raise her concerns about Howard's sacking in a debate next week on the new government's law and order policies.
Howard was the favourite of six candidates who have put themselves up to replace former prime minister John Major, who announced after the May 1 election defeat he would step down.

But Widdecombe's claims that the former home secretary misled the House of Commons -- a grave offence against parliamentary rules -- has sparked bitter accusations and counter-charges and severely dented Howard's chances of victory.
Widdecombe claims Howard misled parliament over the sacking of Derek Lewis as director-general of the prison service -- a decision which Lewis himself has said left Widdecombe in tears.
Howard denies having done anything wrong.

But the temperature of the row soared after Widdecombe was subjected to a barrage of media reports suggesting she had become personally close to Lewis, who the reports said had wooed her with flowers, chocolates and private dinners.
Widdecombe, a 49-year-old spinster and a devout Catholic convert, has angrily denied the reports. But the row has left other leadership candidates uneasy.

Peter Lilley, the former social security secretary and the leadership candidate Widdecombe had publicly backed, criticised her for publicly airing her complaints against Howard and said he would not have her on his leadership team.
